name: Spectral-gap decay and explicit-step (CFL-type) stability for the retained-turbulence relaxation-inertia ODE

statement.latest: \text{Given }\tau_R\dot I_R+L_RI_R=G_R\ (\text{weld/P.05.v1}),\ L_R=L_R^T\succeq0:\ \text{(spectral gap) if }\langle x,L_Rx\rangle\ge\lambda_*\|x\|_2^2\ \forall x\in(\ker L_R)^\perp,\ \text{then}\ \|PI_R(t)\|_2\le e^{-\lambda_*t/\tau_R}\|PI_0\|_2+\frac1{\tau_R}\int_0^te^{-\lambda_*(t-s)/\tau_R}\|PG_R(s)\|_2\,ds;\ \text{(explicit-step stability) for the stepper } I_R^{n+1}=I_R^n+\frac h{\tau_R}(G_R^n-L_RI_R^n),\ A_R:=I-\frac h{\tau_R}L_R,\ \text{if }0\le h\lambda_{\max}/\tau_R\le2\ \text{then}\ \|A_R\|_2\le1\ \text{and}\ \|I_R^N\|_2\le\|I_R^0\|_2+\frac h{\tau_R}\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\|G_R^k\|_2.
statement.note_ascii: Two linear-algebra corollaries of the already-registered retained-turbulence ODE (weld/P.05.v1 via PROP-NS-CONTINUATION-01's continuation result): (1) a spectral-gap estimate -- on the orthogonal complement of ker L_R, the projected retained state decays exponentially at rate lambda_*/tau_R plus a forced term (standard energy/Gronwall-type bound for a positive-semidefinite linear system); (2) an explicit-Euler stepper for the same ODE is non-expansive (||A_R||_2<=1, hence numerically stable) exactly when the step size h obeys the CFL-type bound h*lambda_max/tau_R <= 2, with a companion one-step-residual/finite mismatch metric (eq 33-34 of the source) that is explicitly NOT a continuum singularity criterion. A numerical Euler-stepper convergence check (part of the same source's companion verification script) confirms O(h) convergence consistent with (but not proof of) the stability bound.
statement.provenance_of_check: The O(h) numeric convergence table (source eqs 50-60) is reported by the source as script-verified; this session did not itself re-run that script for this registration -- see honest_caveats.

parents.evidence: Both results are stated for the same retained ODE tau_R dI_R/dt + L_R I_R = G_R already canonical at weld/P.05.v1; this proposal adds a spectral-gap refinement and a discrete-stepper stability analysis of that equation, neither of which is stated in weld/P.05.v1's own entry or in PROP-NS-CONTINUATION-01's registered statement (which stops at global boundedness, not spectral decay rate or a discrete-time stepper).

L_R is the same retained graph-Laplacian-type operator rooted at EQ-008 (L_R := D_W - W) already cited as a parent by the sibling proposal PROP-NS-CONTINUATION-01; the spectral-gap hypothesis (a positive lower bound on <x,L_R x> off ker L_R) is precisely the kind of bound EQ-008's spectral ceiling/floor template is written to supply.

name: Four-layer non-collapse lattice for domain event, adapter failure, retained blow-up, and task breakdown

statement.latest: \text{Let }E_1:=\Sigma_D\text{-event (domain distinction)},\ E_2:=\text{adapter/weld failure},\ E_3:=\Sigma_R(T_*)\text{ (retained-layer blow-up)},\ E_4:=\text{task-level breakdown}.\ \text{Then no pair among }E_1,\dots,E_4\text{ is logically equivalent to another: each }E_i\text{ can occur without the others, given (i) the exact-weld witness of Theorem 3.1/9.1 (}E_1\text{ without }E_2,E_3,E_4\text{) and (ii) the }H_R(T_*)\text{-conditional continuation bound of Theorem 8.1 (}\neg E_3\text{ whenever }H_R(T_*)\text{ holds, independent of }\Sigma_{NS}\text{).}\ \text{Also: bounded }I_R\text{ does not decide task adequacy (Prop.\,10.1), and a }K\text{-Lipschitz reader }O_Q\text{ never blows up if }I_R\text{ stays bounded (Prop.\,10.2).}
statement.note_ascii: A synthesis theorem combining the two already-registered proposals (PROP-NS-WITNESS-01's non-entailment witness as the E1-without-E2 arrow, PROP-NS-CONTINUATION-01's HR-conditional bound as the not-E3 arrow) plus two new supporting propositions: (10.1) a bounded retained state I_R does not by itself decide whether a declared task reader judges the situation adequate/inadequate -- boundedness and task-adequacy are logically independent; (10.2) if the task reader O_Q is K-Lipschitz in I_R, then O_Q cannot blow up while I_R stays bounded (an immediate Lipschitz-continuity corollary). The four-layer lattice (domain event / adapter-weld failure / retained-layer blow-up / task-level breakdown) is asserted to be non-collapsing: none of the four events entails or is entailed by any other in general, using the two prior proposals as its two main supporting arrows plus the two new propositions as auxiliary non-collapse links (E3 vs E4).

coq.print_assumptions: Both theorems: Closed under the global context.

name: Finite-Fourier-mode trace survival through an H^s breakdown time, with weak-L2 reconstruction and spectral defect

statement.latest: \text{For the Fourier-Galerkin projection }u=\sum_ku_k(t)e_k\text{ of (NS), fix }M<\infty.\ \text{Theorem (finite-mode continuation): if }u\in C([0,T_*);H^s),\ s>5/2,\ \text{is a smooth solution on }[0,T_*)\text{ with possible }H^s\text{ breakdown at }T_*,\ \text{then }\lim_{t\uparrow T_*}P_Mu(t)\text{ exists in }H^s\ \forall M<\infty\ \text{(finite-mode separation).}\ \text{Theorem (finite-energy trace, weak L}^2\text{): if }\sum_k\|u_k\|^2_{L^\infty([0,T_*);L^2)}<\infty,\ \text{then }u_k(t)\to u_k^*\text{ as }t\uparrow T_*\ \forall k,\ \text{and }u^*:=\sum_ku_k^*e_k\in L^2\text{ is a well-defined weak trace, with an exact spectral defect }\delta^*:=\lim_M(\|u(t)\|^2_{L^2}-\|P_Mu^*\|^2_{L^2})\text{ localized to high frequencies (}k\to\infty\text{) as }t\uparrow T_*.
statement.note_ascii: The chain: (1) every FIXED Fourier mode of a Galerkin-projected Navier-Stokes solution has a finite limit as t approaches a hypothetical H^s breakdown time T* (each mode's ODE stays regular even if the full H^s norm blows up) -- Volume 3's core result; (2) under an ell^2-summability hypothesis on the mode energies, the full family of per-mode limits assembles into a genuine weak L2 trace u* at T* -- Volume 4's extension beyond fixed-M results; (3) the difference between the true kinetic energy and the energy captured by any fixed finite cutoff M defines an exact spectral defect delta*, which is shown to concentrate at high frequencies as the breakdown time is approached. This bundles Volume 3 (fixed-mode continuation, standard Fourier-Galerkin technique) and Volume 4 (the more complete ell^2/weak-trace/defect construction, which subsumes Volume 3's fixed-M results) into one registered derivation chain, per the survey's recommendation to avoid registering each volume's overlapping restatement separately.

parents.evidence: The finite-mode retained equation for the projected coefficients (source Vol.6 eq 5-11, and the analogous finite-mode ODE underlying Vol.3/4's per-mode continuation) is an explicit instance of the same retained-relaxation-inertia structure already canonical at weld/P.05.v1 -- a fixed-dimension linear/near-linear ODE per Fourier mode, forced by the unresolved nonlinear transfer.

honest_caveats: This is standard applied-PDE technique (Fourier-Galerkin projection, per-mode ODE regularity, ell^2 summability giving weak-L2 convergence) applied within this workspace's readout framing, not novel base mathematics -- the source itself treats the Fourier setup and Galerkin machinery as standard/external (classified 'external/standard' by the Survey phase, not registered here). name: Retained cut-current tape and exact tape-closed finite-mode domain gate (all Readout-Genesis defects exactly zero)

statement.latest: \text{Fix a finite grid }0=t_0<\dots<t_N=T,\ h_n:=t_{n+1}-t_n,\ A_{M,n}:=e^{-h_nL_M}.\ \text{Cut current: }\chi_{M,n}:=\int_{t_n}^{t_{n+1}}e^{-(t_{n+1}-s)L_M}(S_M(s)+\eta_M(s))\,ds.\ \text{Theorem (exact tape-closed recurrence): }I_{M,n+1}=A_{M,n}I_{M,n}+\chi_{M,n},\ \text{so }F^\sharp_{M,n}(I,\chi):=A_{M,n}I+\chi\ \text{is an exact finite update conditioned on the declared tape }T_{M,N}:=(\chi_{M,0},\dots,\chi_{M,N-1}).\ \text{Theorem (exact Readout-Genesis domain gate): }q_{M,n+1}\circ F_{NS,n}=F^\sharp_{M,n}\circ(q_{M,n},\chi_{M,n}),\ O_{M,n}=O^\sharp_{M,n}\circ q_{M,n},\ \text{and with exact arithmetic }\varepsilon_{dyn}=\varepsilon_{read}=\varepsilon_{inv}=0.\ \text{Theorem (future readout sufficiency): }I_{M,n}=I'_{M,n}\ \wedge\ \chi_{M,j}=\chi'_{M,j}\ (n\le j<n+L)\ \Rightarrow\ I_{M,n+r}=I'_{M,n+r}\ (0\le r\le L).
statement.note_ascii: The most structurally novel object in the series: turns the exact-but-not-closed Fourier residual (the unresolved nonlinear transfer between modes) into a DECLARED, dynamically-welded finite quantity -- the 'retained cut-current tape' T_{M,N} -- rather than approximating or discarding it. Once the tape is declared, the finite-mode update becomes an EXACT (not approximate) recurrence conditioned on the tape (Theorem 3.2), and the resulting finite domain exactly satisfies all three Readout-Genesis weld/gate identities (commuting dynamics, matching readout, zero invariant defect) with all three defect terms epsilon_dyn/epsilon_read/epsilon_inv provably zero under exact arithmetic (Theorem 4.1) -- the closest the series comes to a partial, finite-truncated construction of the still-Open q_NS adapter flagged as NSR-02 in Volume 1. Theorem 5.1 shows the resulting finite state plus tape is sufficient (in the technical readout sense) for any future finite-horizon reader.

parents.evidence: The cut-current tape T_{M,N} reuses the same append-only-tape/record-retention concept already canonical under the EQ-015 root (the workspace's general append-only tape T_n construction, cited in Volume 1's own T-CAN-002/003 citations of EQ-015/M.01.v1 and M.02.v1); this proposal is a domain-specific instance of that general tape concept, applied to Fourier-mode cut currents rather than a generic record sequence.

Theorem 4.1's 'exact Readout-Genesis domain gate' (eq 21-23: q_{M,n+1} o F_{NS,n} = F^#_{M,n} o (q_{M,n}, chi_{M,n}), and the readout-commuting identity) is an explicit instantiation of the CAN-006 weld schema (canonical at weld/M.02.v1) for this specific finite-mode/tape-closed domain, with all three defect terms exactly zero rather than merely bounded.

The variation-of-constants recurrence I_{M,n+1}=A_{M,n}I_{M,n}+chi_{M,n} is the same retained-ODE machinery already canonical at weld/P.05.v1 (and used by PROP-NS-CONTINUATION-01), specialized to a declared finite time grid with the residual forcing folded into the explicit tape term chi_{M,n} rather than left as an unresolved continuous forcing.

Tier is Dr, not Th_coqc, pending an actual compiling axiom-free Coq proof.

name: Readout-Navier-Stokes Discrete Crossing Theorem (H^3 continuum breakdown does not imply finite tape-closed readout breakdown)

statement.latest: \text{Define }\Sigma_{H^3}(1):=\mathbf1_{\limsup_{t\uparrow1}\|u(t)\|_{H^3}=\infty},\ \text{Break}_M(1):=\mathbf1_{\{I_M(1^-),I_M(1),I_M(1^+)\ \text{do not agree}\}}.\ \text{Theorem (Readout-Navier-Stokes discrete crossing): under Assumption 1, for every fixed }M<\infty:\ \Sigma_{H^3}(1)=1\ \wedge\ \text{Break}_M(1)=0.\ \text{Hence } H^3\text{ continuum breakdown} \;\not\Rightarrow\; \text{finite tape-closed readout breakdown}.\ \text{Corollary (all fixed finite cutoffs survive): }\forall M<\infty,\ \text{Break}_M(1)=0.
statement.note_ascii: The series' capstone/headline theorem. Combines: (i) the candidate's own assumed continuum H^3 blow-up at t=1 (an external hypothesis, Assumption 1, mirroring OpenAI's stated construction); (ii) weak L2 continuity of the finite-mode trace (from PROP-NS-FOURIER-TRACE-01's chain); and (iii) the exact tape-closed domain's zero-defect closure (from PROP-NS-TAPE-CLOSED-DOMAIN-01) to conclude that, for every FIXED finite mode cutoff M, the retained finite state does not register any discontinuity at the moment of continuum breakdown, when the unresolved nonlinear transfer is retained explicitly as an exact tape rather than discarded or approximated. This does not resolve the continuum Clay problem; it is a statement entirely about what a class of finite readers can and cannot see.
